20 Best Things To Do This Weekend In Singapore – 23rd-25th October 2026

Things to do this weekend in Singapore

Kid-friendly activities, live performances, and fun workshops – there’s plenty of fun to be had in the coming weeks. So, open your calendars and bookmark these things to do this weekend in Singapore.

1. DINOSAUR ODYSSEY T-Rex Walkabout

23rd-25th Oct


Image for illustration purposes only.
Image credit: Resorts World Sentosa

ADVERTISEMENT

If your little one is utterly obsessed with dinosaurs, bring them out to come face-to-face with a mighty prehistoric beast at the DINOSAUR ODYSSEY T-Rex Walkabout. Happening at 6 locations across the island from 23rd to 25th October 2026, there’ll be plenty of opportunities to get up close with the lifelike dino as it roars to life.

The DINOSAUR ODYSSEY T-Rex Walkabout will be held at the following locations:

Date Location & times
23rd Oct, Fri Changi Airport Jewel: 2pm, 3.15pm, 4.30pm
Westgate: 7.30pm. 8.30pm
24th Oct, Sat Waterway Point: 11.30am, 12.30pm
Our Tampines Hub: 3.30pm, 4.30pm, 5.30pm
The Bricks (Choa Chu Kang Ave 7, Opp Blk 810 CP): 8.30pm
25th Oct, Sun Waterway Point: 11am, 12pm
Choa Chu Kang Community Club: 6.15pm

Do note that the session at The Bricks and Choa Chu Kang CC are ticketed events; tickets cost $7 and $5 respectively and can be bought at the entrance.

 

ADVERTISEMENT

Those who spot the T-Rex at 3 or more locations will also be duly rewarded. Post your sightings on social media, tag them with @season_entertainment_asia, and you’ll receive a set of 6 dinosaur plushies. Dino lovers who catch the T-Rex at all 6 locations can redeem an exclusive DINO-A-LIVE booklet, a large dinosaur plush, and the same set of 6 smaller plushies.

Admission: Free, with 2 ticketed locations
Venue: Various locations around Singapore
Date: 23rd-25th October 2026
Time: Varies from location

2. Movies by the Beach

24th Oct-1st Nov


Image credit: Sentosa

ADVERTISEMENT

Upgrade movie nights with a visit to Sentosa, because just a monorail ride away is Movies by the Beach. Located at the Palawan Kidz City Roof Garden and Fort Siloso, it’s where you can enjoy flicks for free, under a canopy of stars. Simply break out a picnic mat and get cosy; this time, there’ll even be horror movies screening to close out Halloween weekend.

Date Movie
24th Oct, Sat Night at the Museum (2006), PG
25th Oct, Sun Dora and the Lost City of Gold (2019), PG
31st Oct, Sat Happy Death Day (2017), PG13
1st Nov, Sun Happy Death Day 2U (2019), PG13

Admission: Free
Venue: Sentosa, Palawan Kidz City Roof Garden & Fort Siloso
Date: 24rd October-1st November 2026
Time: 7pm, Daily

ADVERTISEMENT

3. Tampines 1 Halloween Scaretacular 2026

22nd-25th, 29th-31st Oct & 1st Nov

Easties, you won’t have to stray far from home to get your fair share of frights. Tampines 1’s rooftop is playing host to the Halloween Scaretacular 2026, where you’ll have to find your way out of a gamified maze filled with suspense around every corner. Try to keep your nerve as you uncover clues to solve puzzles, all while being spooked by scare actors that are way too faithful to their roles.

Tickets cost $10/pax, but you can also accumulate a minimum spend of $100 at the mall to redeem 2 free tickets, or $150 to redeem 4 tickets.

Admission: $10/pax
Venue: 10 Tampines Central 1, Tampines 1, Rooftop, Singapore 529536
Date: 22nd-25th, 29th-31st October & 1st November 2026
Time: 7pm-11pm, Daily

4. Singapore Car Expo

24th-25th Oct

Whether you’re in the market for your first set of wheels or looking for an upgrade, the Singapore Car Expo is where you’d wanna be to get the best deals around. All the biggest names in the automotive game will be showcasing their latest models and promotions, so expect to stop by booths by brands such as BYD, Tesla, BMW, and Toyota to name a few.

Image credit: The Car Expo via Facebook

What’s more, the first 1,000 visitors will receive a free film camera, while the first 30 to spend at least $80 on car accessories can redeem a $10 SPC cash voucher. For those who buy a car at the expo, you stand a chance to win up to $1,000 in SPC cash vouchers, so you won’t have to worry about fuel expenses for your new ride for quite a while.

Admission: Free
Venue: 1 Expo Drive, Singapore Expo, Halls 5 & 6, Singapore 486150
Date: 24th-25th October 2026
Time: 10pm-9pm, Daily

5. Weekend Brew Club

24th-25th Oct

Image for illustration purposes only.
Image credit: Weekend Brew Club 

The Weekend Brew Club is bringing back its beloved coffee buffet and nostalgic activities, and this time, they’ll be stationed in the West, at Boon Lay Place Block 207’s hard court. Although you’ll need a ticket to enjoy free-flow beverages like espressos and cafe lattes, you can still take part in their game booths.

Some you can roll up your sleeves for include Mahjong Wall and Mahjong Winning Hand challenges, and be sure to stick around for rounds of carrom too. They’ve also got a free terrarium workshop to sit in for, while the live DJ performances make sure you’ll want to stick around for a bit

Admission: Free
Venue: 207 Boon Lay Place, Singapore 640207
Date: 24th-25th October 2026
Time: Sat 11am-6pm | Sun 9am-4pm

6. The Secret Vault by the GIC

10th Oct-1st Nov

Picture this: you’re dashing through a hypermart with a shopping list, except the price tags keep changing before you can make it to the cashier. That’s just 1 of the challenges waiting at The Secret Vault, a free, limited-time event at New Bahru‘s School Hall.

Put together by GIC, the global institutional investor that manages Singapore’s foreign reserves, it spans 6 interactive chambers that each drop you into a different world.

At The Global Inflation Hypermart, you’ll race against the clock to fill your cart as prices keep climbing, and get a first-hand feel for just how quickly inflation eats into the value of your money. Over at The Steward’s Gardens, you’ll navigate a dark maze filled with hidden risks before picking up an actual watering can to grow your own digital flowers. There’s also The Weather Room, where the environment around you shifts with every breaking headline.

Between the ticking timers and moody lighting, there’s plenty to keep you on your toes, plus plenty of cool shots for the ‘Gram. By the time you leave the vault, you’ll have a newfound appreciation for how Singapore’s reserves have weathered both good times and rough patches over the past 45 years. And who knows? You may very well feel inspired to join GIC’s mission in securing Singapore’s financial future.

Promo: Ride to The Secret Vault in comfort with $2 off your TADA Ride to New Bahru when you key in the code <GICVAULT>, T&Cs apply.

Register now to secure your slot to visit The Secret Vault.

Admission: Free
Venue: 46 & 58 Kim Yam Road, New Bahru School Hall, Level 2, Singapore 239351
Date: 10th October-1st November 2026
Time: Mon 12pm-6pm | Tue-Thu 11am-7pm | Fri-Sun 11am-8pm

7. Crack The Case: Wonderland at Goodman Arts Centre

Now till 1st Nov 2026

If you’re all about solving mysteries and riddles, Crack The Case: Wonderland might just be for you. Designed as a 90-minute immersive detective and theatre experience, expect to play an active role in piecing together puzzles with clues from the characters of Wonderland as you solve the mystery of the Mad Hatter’s missing hat.

Image credit: Abigail Buligan 

Running at Goodman Arts Centre, this is the latest edition of the “Crack The Case” series by Sight Lines Entertainment. There’s also an add-on activity, the Wonderland Children’s Workshop, which starts before the show and is sure to delight the little ones. The whole experience is also SG Culture Pass-eligible, so here’s your chance to experience a theatre show in a new light, potentially for free.

Get tickets to Crack The Case: Wonderland.

Admission: From $88/pax
Venue: 90 Goodman Road, Goodman Arts Centre Blackbox, Singapore 439053
Date: Now until 1st Nov 2026
Time: 10.30am, 2pm for Family-friendly shows | 4.45pm, 8pm for Adults

8. American Tourister The Great Gourmet Getaway

9th Oct-30th Nov


Image credit: American Tourister

If you’re gearing up for your next trip, you can warm up with a food trail closer to home. American Tourister has launched The Great Gourmet Getaway, a gastronomical experience taking you through 5 of Singapore’s beloved F&B spots: Birds of Paradise, Chimichanga, Cowpresso, Dumpling Darlings, and Two Men Bagel House. Each stop serves a limited-time, special American Tourister curated menu, and you’ll stamp your way through the trail to unlock sure-win rewards.

Complete the stamp card and you’ll also be in the running for The Great Giveaway, with prizes worth $200 up for grabs. To qualify, you’ll need to buy a Getaway with American Tourister luggage bundle, visit all 5 food partners, and order the curated menus at each one.


Image credit: American Tourister

The bundles start from $199 with the Argyle, which is scratch-resistant and has a multi-pocket interior, plus QUIETO wheels for quiet, smooth gliding. The Tranto, from $299, is a multi-opening spinner that lets you pack how you want, even in tight spaces, with a quick-access front pocket and Optimov shock-absorbing wheels with StePause technology for better control and stability.

Find out more about The Great Gourmet Getaway.

Locations: Various Birds of Paradise, Chimichanga, Cowpresso, Dumpling Darlings & Two Men Bagel House outlets across Singapore
Date: 9th October to 30th November 2026

9. Our Schools, Our Stories Photo & Video Exhibition

14th-25th Oct


Image credit: Ministry of Education

Most parents only hear about their kids’ school day in one-word answers over dinner. Organised by MOE, the Our Schools, Our Stories Photo & Video Exhibition certainly helps to fill in the rest. This year’s event marks the 9th edition, drawing 2,888 entries across 277 schools. The snaps and clips aren’t just taken by students, but even by teachers and school staff who are part and parcel of their everyday experience.

Even if you’re not a parent of a little one currently in school, we highly recommend this exhibition just to bask in nostalgia, and reminisce about a simpler time. Seeing snippets of school life through someone else’s lens tends to bring back the little things, like recess queues, bags that were far too heavy, and corridors that were never quiet.


Image credit: Ministry of Education

Besides getting to admire all the photos and videos on display, there’ll also be a treasure hunt across the different zones, where the clues are hidden among the showcased stories. Solve it to redeem prizes such as a key chain or plushie.

Find out more about the Our Schools, Our Stories Photo & Video Exhibition.

Admission: Free
Venue: 100 Victoria Street, National Library Building, The Plaza, Singapore 188064
Date: 14th-25th Oct
Time: 12pm-8pm

10. Toy Story | PEACEMINUSONE: The First Fan pop-up

16th Oct till 11th Nov

 

Head on over to the Toy Story | PEACEMINUSONE: The First Fan pop-up for a piece of G-Dragon’s unbridled, yet playful creativity. The King of K-pop’s fashion and lifestyle brand PEACEMINUSONE has joined hands with Disney’s Toy Story to bring fans of all ages a world of whimsy over at CQ @ Clarke Quay.

You’ll be able to snap pics with Woody and gang, who’re all impeccably dressed in special get-ups that sport the Korean brand’s iconic sunflower motif. Of course, you can’t go home without a memento, so be sure to cart out merch such as keychains, plushies, figurines, hats, tees, and tote bags featuring beloved characters like Buzz, Jessie, Bullseye, and Rex.

Get tickets to Toy Story | PEACEMINUSONE: The First Fan pop-up.

Admission: $12/pax
Venue: 3A River Valley Road, CQ @ Clarke Quay, #01-02
Date: 16th October-11th November 2026
Time: 1pm-11pm, Daily

11. Deepavali Open House

17th Oct-8th Nov

Image credit: Indian Heritage Centre 

The Indian Heritage Centre is kickstarting the Deepavali festivities ahead of time with their annual Deepavali Open House. It’s free for all to pop by to experience the wonders of the festival of light, and it’s packed with plenty of family-friendly activities, perfect for filling out a weekend or 2.

Image credit: Indian Heritage Centre 

For maximum immersion, try on a community-loaned saree and strike a pose at the vintage photobooth on-site. Meanwhile, the creative minds can have a go at a couple of hands-on workshops, such as clay brooch painting and putting together your very own mini mithai box. A weekend bazaar will also be set up where you can bring home festive treats and accessories.

Admission: Free
Venue: 5 Campbell Lane, Indian Heritage Centre, Singapore 209924
Date: Weekends from 17th October-8th November 2026
Time: Sat 10am-8pm | 10am-6pm Sun

12. Singapore Dog Festival

23rd-25th, 30th-31st Oct & 1st Nov

Image credit: Singapore Dog Festival

The Singapore Dog Festival is happening at Palawan Green in Sentosa over 3 weekends, and it’s where you’ll want to be if you’ve got an energetic pupper in tow. Your furry friend will have a field day at the Colossal Sensory Garden playscape, featuring massive flora and winding pathways to trot down, a nod to the regular-sized Sensoryscape just nearby.

Image credit: Singapore Dog Festival

Other than sitting in for expert talks and tuning in to live stage performances, you can even sign you and your furkid up for a Dog Pilates session ($12) by Soulevé on 25th October and 1st November 2026. Afterwards, head over to the curated marketplace to shop for treats and pet essentials, and remember to come in costume for a flurry of spooky activities on Halloween weekend.

Get tickets for the Singapore Dog Festival.

Admission: $7/adult | $4/child
Venue: Siloso Beach Walk, Palawan Green, Sentosa
Date: 23rd-25th, 30th-31st October & 1st November 2026
Time: 3pm-9pm, Daily

13. Haw Ror Villa 5! – Back From The Dead

Now till 15th Nov

Should the crowd at USS’ Halloween Horror Night prove to be too frightening, Haw Par Villa’s annual scare fest is a good alternative. Dubbed Haw Ror Villa, it has returned to haunt Hell’s Museum for the 5th year running; make no mistake, it still packs a punch frights-wise, making it just the haunt for horror fans.

It’s split into 4 zones, each themed differently and chock-full with suspense around every corner. Zone 1 serves as a precursor to the horrors ahead, as a court official from the 10 Courts of Hell sets the stage with an immersive performance. You’ll make your way through the Gateway of Hell in Zone 2, which is fraught with jumpscares, on top and puzzles to solve for an interactive experience.

On that note, we’ll leave you to find out the rest of the perils that await. It takes around 2 to 2.5 hours to finish exploring all 4 zones, so we recommend having a decent meal before setting foot into this otherworldly attraction. FYI, you can pay for admission tickets to Haw Ror Villa 5! with your SG Culture Pass credits.

Get tickets to Haw Ror Villa 5! – Back From The Dead.

Admission: From $55/pax
Venue: 262 Pasir Panjang Road, Haw Par Villa, Singapore 118628
Date: Now till 15th November 2026
Time: 6.30pm-12am, Daily

14. Sunflower Surprise: Garden by the Ocean

Now till 9th Nov


Image credit: Gardens by the Bay

This October, Gardens by the Bay is debuting its very first Portuguese-themed floral display Sunflower Surprise: Garden by the Ocean. No prizes for guessing which flower they’ll be spotlighting in this one; a sea of over 5,000 sunflowers across 20 varieties will engulf the Flower Dome, as the display faithfully recreates the country’s quaint coastal towns and picturesque countryside.


Image credit: Gardens by the Bay

Expect to wander through a replica of Alfama, one of Lisbon’s oldest neighbourhoods, snap pics by the striped houses of the Costa Nova fishing village, complete with a 6m-tall Farol de Belém lighthouse. You’ll also get to catch a glimpse of Portugal’s agricultural traditions, by exploring vineyards, olive groves, and cork oaks.

Admission: From $12/adult | $8/child & senior
Venue: 18 Marina Gardens Drive, Gardens by the Bay, Flower Dome Singapore 018953
Date: 9th October-9th November 2026
Time: 9am-9pm

15. Bollywood Farms

Now till 31st Dec

We’ll have to unfortunately wave goodbye to an iconic Primary School excursion destination pretty soon, as Bollywood Farms will be shuttering at the end of 2026. As such, take this chance to reminisce about the good ol’ days by swinging for one last look at the idyllic attraction.

We did just that, and found that there’s plenty to see, do, and eat. Explore the 10-acre farm by embarking on a self-guided trail, on which you’ll be able to see their vegetable gardens and fruit-bearing trees. Snap pics by the lotus pond, one of the largest of its kind in Singapore, and frolic amongst the butterflies at the butterfly garden.

Conclude your visit with a pit stop at the farm’s Poison Ivy Bistro, which whips up hearty servings of local delights such as Nasi Lemak and Nasi Ulam. Of course, all veggies used for their dishes here are all harvested right from the nearby gardens.

16. Bellygom Summer Day Out 2026

18th Sep-1st Nov

After taking over Changi Airport for a bit earlier this year, the lovable Bellygom will be blessing Waterway Point with its pink presence starting this weekend, all the way till 1st November 2026. Dubbed Bellygom Summer Day Out, this 1.5-month-long celebration will feature plenty of Bellygom-themed experiences that the whole fam can enjoy.

Start out at the Bellygom Chill Out Zone at the mall’s The Plaza, which will be decked out with pool floats for the perfect summer-inspired photoshoot. Over at The Cove, you’ll be able to pick up Bellygom merch, have a go at interactive games, and snap even more pics with whimsical photo spots.

For the kids, a huge Bellygom Inflatable Fun playground awaits them at the Village Square. Simply hit a minimum spend of $30 at the mall for 25 minutes of playtime. Speaking of which, rack up a minimum spend of $150, or $200 on supermarket transactions, in 3 same-day transactions to redeem a Bellygom Shopping Bag from now till 8th October 2026.

Admission: Free
Venue: 83 Punggol Central, Waterway Point, Singapore 828761
Date: 18th September to 1st November 2026

17. Halloween Horror Nights 14

25th Sep-1st Nov

Kickstarting spooky szn this weekend is Universal Studios Singapore’s Halloween Horror Nights 14. Singapore’s largest scare fest is welcoming visitors once again, and this year’s theme is centred around the unassuming Karang Guni Man. A total of 4 new haunted houses, 3 live shows, and 2 scare zones await you if you’re game.

We won’t spoil too much, but expect to explore a Karang Guni’s shop that’s infested with cursed wares, find your way out of a decrepit recording studio with a dark past, and tune in to the fan-favourite Scaremony to set the mood for the frights ahead.

Get tickets to Halloween Horror Nights 14.

Admission: From $68/pax
Venue: 8 Sentosa Gateway, Universal Studios Singapore, 098269
Date: Select nights between 25th September-1st November 2026
Time: 7.30pm-12.30am

18. Respite with LAC at Absolute Pilates

26th Oct-1st Nov


Image credit: LAC & Absolute

If spooky season has you running from one scare fest to the next, consider pencilling in a slower weekend for a change. Supplement brand LAC has teamed up with Absolute Pilates for Respite with LAC, a week-long wellness programme running across all 5 Absolute studios in Singapore. The focus here is on rest and recovery rather than chasing personal bests, with Reformer Pilates classes meant to help you slow down and recharge.

Those new to both brands can snag a 2-for-1 package at $55, which gets you 2 classes. To unlock it, sign up for LAC’s e-newsletter, or show proof of your LAC membership at any Absolute studio. Class credits stay valid for 1 month, so you won’t have to cram both sessions into the same week. Existing Absolute members can simply book participating classes with their current packages.

Either way, you’ll leave with a LAC Mobility Trial Kit of product samples and promos, which you can redeem via a QR code at the front desk.

Find out more about Respite with LAC.

Admission: $55 for 2 classes
Venue: Various Absolute studios across Singapore
Date: 26th October-1st November 2026
Time: Varies by class schedule

– New shows, concerts & exhibitions in Singapore this week –

19. ONE Ocean: Every Action Ripples

Now till 3rd Jan 2027

Make waves this June at Science Centre Singapore with a lineup of immersive science experiences for the whole fam. The big highlight is ONE Ocean: Every Action Ripples, a new multi-sensory exhibition opening on 30th May that takes visitors on a deep-sea adventure through 10 interactive zones featuring 360° ocean projections, free-roaming VR, spatial soundscapes, and hands-on installations.

Expect everything from Arctic expeditions and coral reefs to whale migrations and Singapore’s own marine ecosystems, all wrapped up in a visually stunning experience that feels part science museum, part underwater fever dream.

There’ll also be ocean-themed activities under JUNEureka 2026, special KidsSTOP™ programmes, and school holiday activities happening throughout the month.

Get tickets for ONE Ocean: Every Action Ripples.

Admission: $18/adult | $13/child
Venue: Science Centre Singapore, Annexe Halls
Dates: From 30th May onwards
Time: Tue-Sun 10am-5pm

20. Into the Ocean: Journey Beneath

6th Jun-1st Nov

Another journey into the depths of the ocean starts at the ArtScience Museum this June. As its name suggests, Into the Ocean: Journey Beneath is a new exhibition where visitors can get a glimpse into life beneath the crashing waves.

First, you’ll step into an OceanX’s research vessel to simulate an actual deep-sea expedition, where sound, visuals, interactive technology and even scent will paint a vivid picture of what marine biologists encounter during real missions. Admire specimens of coral reef and sea-dwelling animals, and snap a pic at the pretty Lucida light installation that’s meant to mimic the sensation of being surrounded by shifting currents.

Admission: From $19.50-/adult | $16.50/child
Venue: 6 Bayfront Avenue, ArtScience Museum Singapore 018974
Dates: 6th June-1st November 2026
Time: Sun-Thu 10am-7pm | Fri-Sat 10am-9pm

Find things to do in Singapore this weekend

We’re sure you have more than enough activities to fill your upcoming weekend. If not, check out our ultimate list of things to do in Singapore or the best attractions and activities in Singapore. If you’re looking for pretty places to snap lots of photos, hit up these Instagrammable places in Singapore while you’re at it.

And those looking to plan their calendars in advance can check out our full list of upcoming live performances in 2026.
